title: Looks in one place: wireframes
intro: Where recipes, film stocks and Base Looks show in Develop, today and after LKS-12: drawn from the code on main (3b9c0f17) and the owner's decisions of 13 October 2026.
reading: Boxes are regions, numbers point to the notes under each wireframe, and counts are real except for your own recipes and imports. A dimmed row with › is a folder, and ▮ stands for a film's icon: a canister, slide mount, reel or print in the stock's colours. Every region says where it stands:

building.label: Being built
building.meaning: Being built in this workstream (LKS-12) now.

planned.label: Planned
planned.meaning: In this workstream's plan, not started yet.

you.label: Waits on you
you.meaning: Waits on one of the questions.

flow.title: Find a look on the left
flow.text: Browse the Recipes panel's folders or search it. Film rows show their film's icon; search also lists Base Looks.

flow.title: Hover to preview
flow.text: Every row previews on the photo as the pointer rests on it, as today.

flow.title: Click to apply
flow.text: A film stock brings its grain, halation and bloom; right-click › Apply Base Look Only brings its colour alone.

flow.title: See and adjust it on the right
flow.text: Basic › Base Look shows the look in use, first and checked, with its Amount; its menu lists only Fixer's looks, the Film Styles and Reproduction.

principles.title: Each look in one place
principles.text: A look that comes as a recipe is listed only in the Recipes panel; the Base Look menu lists the looks that have no recipe of their own.

principles.title: The left finds, the right shows
principles.text: The Recipes panel is where you search, browse and apply; the Base Look is the one look under every slider, as Lightroom's Profile.

principles.title: Hover keeps previewing
principles.text: Recipe rows, Base Look rows in search, the browser's tiles and the Film Looks window's cards all preview on hover.

principles.title: Nothing renders differently
principles.text: Edits keep the looks they have; one whose Base Look is a film stock shows it at the top of the menu.

screens.name: Today
screens.title: Where looks are today
screens.summary: The same 36 film names appear on both sides and do different things: the left applies the film with its effects, the right its colour alone. A third place, the Film Looks window, shows the left's recipes again as cards.

notes.title: Recipes panel
notes.text: Search, the applied recipe's Amount, then folders: the 39 starter recipes in eight groups, Film Stocks (36) and Mood (20), plus your lists and imports. Rows show a name, a star or a cube; no icons. Hover previews, click applies.

notes.title: Base Look menu
notes.text: About 60 entries: In This Photo, Fixer (6), Film Stocks (36, with icons), Film Styles (15), Fujifilm LUTs, Installed, Reproduction; then Browse Base Looks… and Film Looks…. No hover preview in the menu.

notes.title: Browse Base Looks…
notes.text: A 420 × 520 popover with every Base Look as a thumbnail of the photo, by the same sections; hover previews the look alone. The Recipe Cards switches for imported Fujifilm LUTs (RCP-31) sit at its foot.

notes.title: Film Looks window
notes.text: ⇧⌘L: the 36 film recipes as large cards with kind tabs, favourites, ⌥ for the photo before, hover to preview, click to apply with grain, halation and bloom.

tables.title: Each kind of look, and where it shows
rows: Film Stocks: look, grain, halation, bloom
Film Stocks: colour only, with icons

screens.name: Recipes panel
screens.title: The Recipes panel
screens.summary: Where every look is found and applied, browsing (left) and searching for "chrome" (right).

lists.note: CineStill 800T is under the pointer: the photo previews it.

regions.label: Film icons
regions.text: ▮ before a row: its film's icon, at the row's size.

lists.note: Chrome is a Film Style: hover previews the look alone, click sets the Base Look.
Highlighted: the photo shows CineStill 800T's colour without its halation.

notes.title: Search finds Base Looks too
notes.text: Recipes first, then the Base Looks that match, under their own heading: Fixer's six, the Film Styles, Reproduction and the photo's own. Hovering one previews the look alone; clicking sets only the Base Look. The words profile, base and look list them all.

notes.title: Film icons
notes.text: Each film row shows its film's icon at the panel's row size, drawn by FilmIcon and found by LookIcons. Whether the moods and your own recipes built on a film show it too is question 2.

notes.title: Film Stocks, once
notes.text: The 36 films, the only place they're listed. The order is question 1. Hover previews the film with its effects, as today; click applies it.

notes.title: A recipe's menu
notes.text: Apply Base Look Only, for every recipe with a Base Look, sets its look and leaves the rest of the edit. While it's highlighted, the photo previews the look alone.

notes.title: The Film Stocks folder's menu
notes.text: Open Film Looks opens the window of cards, besides Window › Film Looks and ⇧⌘L.

screens.name: Base Look
screens.title: Basic › Base Look
screens.summary: The one look under every slider, as Lightroom's Profile: here after CineStill 800T was applied from the Recipes panel.

blocks.note: Recipe Cards: Chrome uses your imported LUT

notes.title: The look in use, first
notes.text: When the photo's look came from a recipe (a film stock or an imported LUT), it's listed first, checked, with its icon. Otherwise the check sits in its own section.

notes.title: Only looks with no recipe of their own
notes.text: In This Photo, Fixer (6), Film Styles (15), Installed looks no recipe uses, and Reproduction. Film Stocks and Fujifilm LUTs are gone; they're recipes. The ⌘K Base Looks page lists the same.

notes.title: Amount
notes.text: The Base Look's Amount, 0 to 200, unchanged.

notes.title: Browse Base Looks…
notes.text: The same sections as thumbnails, the photo's look first. Every tile previews on hover, as today. The Recipe Cards switches stay at its foot.

notes.title: Film Looks… leaves the menu
notes.text: Films aren't Base Look entries any more; the window opens from the Recipes panel, the Window menu and ⇧⌘L.

screens.name: Hover
screens.title: Where hovering previews
screens.summary: The pointer resting on a look shows it on the photo, without applying it, wherever a look is listed. The Base Look menu itself doesn't preview, as today. If the editor can't redraw while a menu is open, holding ⌥ over a recipe row previews its look alone instead of the highlighted menu item.

questionsIntro: Each changes parts that aren't built yet. Say which you'd like, or anything you'd change on the other tabs.

questions.title: How are the 36 film stocks ordered in the Recipes panel?
questions.now: Today's order lists the variants (Portra 400 · +2, Tri-X pushed, the prints, bleach bypass, cross-processed) at the end, away from their stocks.
options: One list by kind (colour negative, cinema, slide, black and white), each variant beside its stock; the Film Looks window the same
Four subfolders by kind, as the Film Looks window's tabs
questions.lean: One list by kind with the variants beside their stocks: hovering down one list keeps working, and the icons show the kind.

questions.title: Which recipe rows show a film icon?
questions.now: No recipe row shows an icon today; the Base Look menu and browser show film icons.
options: Every recipe whose Base Look is a film stock: the film stocks, the moods and your own recipes built on one
questions.lean: Every recipe built on a film: Golden Leak then shows it's Portra, until the moods get icons of their own.

questions.title: What icon does a look that isn't a film stock get?
questions.now: None yet. The sheet ~/src/fixer/build/icons/look-icon-styles.png (fixer recipe icons --styles) draws each style on four looks at the app's sizes. Scene objects read at every size; mood marks read when the mark is a frame or a halo, and a light leak barely shows; chips of one photo look alike at list sizes, since the photo outweighs the look.
options: The mood's mark on its film's icon (Golden Leak: the Portra canister with a warm leak; Summer '98: a print border)
An object for the scene (Golden Hour: a low sun; Blue Hour: a street lamp; Soft Skin: a portrait)
A chip rendered from the look itself, which also works for your own recipes and imported LUTs
questions.lean: Scene objects for the starter recipes and mood marks (frames and halos, not leaks) for the moods: both read at 16 pt, and chips don't. The style you pick becomes a tracker row.
questions.answer: B, scene objects, with Golden Hour's low sun as the direction for now (LKS-14). The existing film icons don't change. (13 October)

questions.title: Where does each film stock live?
questions.answer: Once, in the Recipes panel, with its film icon. Clicking applies the colour with grain, halation and bloom; right-click › Apply Base Look Only. The Base Look menu and browser stop listing film stocks and imported LUTs, showing one only while it's the photo's look. (13 October)

questions.title: Where do Fixer's looks and the Film Styles live?
questions.answer: On the right, in a short Base Look menu, and the Recipes panel's search finds them too, listed after the recipes. (13 October)

questions.title: Does hovering still preview?
questions.answer: Yes, everywhere a look is listed. The browser and the Film Looks window both stay; a film's colour alone previews while Apply Base Look Only is highlighted. (13 October)

questions.title: Icons for more looks?
questions.answer: A skill, fixer-look-icons, for more film stock icons and other kinds that convey a look's mood. (13 October)
